_comment: The graphs inside core's `library` sub-graph (`core-library-graph` in `folio-assistant-core.json`), declared FROM WITHIN (#980) on the pattern of cat-harness's `library/graph.json`. The corpus alone is OPT-IN (`optIn: true`), off in every layer unless that layer lists `folio-assistant-core.library` in its own `enableSubgraphs` (owner, 2026-11-10, card Q-SG-3 option A). Its id stays `library`, so core's own ingestion resolves its corpus under the conventional id. A switched-off from-within entry is not promoted, so a layer above keeps its own `library` or the built-in default. References inside the sources keep the logical `library/<slug>` spelling, as cat-harness's corpus does.
name: library

directories.description: L1 source content this LAYER owns — the publications core's own vocabulary and methods are derived FROM, one `<bib-slug>/` per ingested document. Declared rather than borrowed because a method is placed by OWNERSHIP (`methodology-adoption` §4): a paper core's methodology cites from another layer's library would not lift out with it. Holds Doc-Researcher (`arxiv-2510.21603v1`), the C2PA Technical Specification 2.5 (`c2pa-2026-specification-2-5`, CC-BY-4.0) and the DSpace 7 REST Contract (`dspace-7-rest-contract`, BSD-3-Clause). `ingest-document.ts` refuses to guess a destination when several are declared. `dependents: skip` because these are THIS layer's sources; a downstream folio's library is its own. The id is the CONVENTIONAL `library` since 2026-11-04 (owner, card 'Library rule' option 1): cat-harness's corpus became opt-in inside its `library` sub-graph, so the convention a layer above inherits — a `library/` of its own, by id and relative path (bean `wwi6`) — now comes from this layer, the one that owns content, as this entry's earlier text on cat-harness said it should. It was `core-library` until then, so as not to shadow the harness's entry. Moved to `library/corpus/` on 2026-11-10 (card Q-SG-3 option A).
